subject: Analysis of Measurement Invariance with multiple imputed data and categorical variables

messages.author: 93e4893e69ec8930
messages.subject: Analysis of Measurement Invariance with multiple imputed data and categorical variables
parts:
Hi all,

 

Background: I have been working on developing some scales for the educational domain. Items are categorical. Upon completion of the survey, I also want to run some tests of measurement invariances. Here, I follow the procedure proposed by Wu and Estabrook (2016). Hence, I estimate a baseline (configural) model, then a threshold model and then a model on metric invariance (i.e., threshold and loadings constrained to be equal across groups). To do so, I basically adjusted the codes provided by Svetina et al. (2020). I had to adjust them to account for the multiple imputations I compiled due to missingness in the data. As it is common, to do so I used mice and thus run all MI models using the cfa.mi command.

 

Problem: Executing this procedure, I get results that I cannot explain let alone understand. In short, the baseline and the thresholds models do not differ at all in terms of the fit indices and even in terms of df. This is unexpected. Since in the latter model thresholds are constrained to be equal across groups, the degrees of freedoms should go up. I also run the same MI analysis for the factor model chosen across different school subjects and my weird results replicate consistently. Basically, my questions are what went wrong and how to fix it?

 

The implementation: The general model chosen for the MI analysis is as follows:

 

library(lavaan)

library(semTools)

 

MODEL <-  '

C_AB =~  C_AB2 + C_AB3 + C_AB4 + C_AB5 + C_AB6 + C_AB8

C_VA =~  C_DA1 + C_DA2 + C_DA3 + C_GE1 + C_GE2 + C_GE3 + C_GE4 + C_GE5

C_CO =~  C_AB7 + C_EF2 + C_EF3 + C_EF5 + C_NE2 + C_NE4'

 

the ordered variables are:

VAR <-   c("C_AB2", "C_AB3", "C_AB4", "C_AB5", "C_AB6", "C_AB8",

                  "C_DA1", "C_DA2", "C_DA3", "C_GE1", "C_GE2", "C_GE3", "C_GE4", "C_GE5",

                   "C_AB7", "C_EF2", "C_EF3", "C_EF5", "C_NE2", "C_NE4")

 

As a first step, I used measEq.syntax to generate the lavaan MI model syntax. This model was then estimated:

 

baseline <- measEq.syntax(configural.model = MODEL,

                            ordered = VAR,

                            data = BASELINE_IMP_EX_1,

                            parameterization = "delta",

                            ID.fac = "std.lv",

                            ID.cat = "Wu.Estabrook.2016",

                            group = "Sex",

                            group.equal = "configural")

 

model.baseline <- as.character(baseline)  

 

BASELINE.FIT <- cfa.mi(model.baseline,

                         data=BASELINE_IMP_EX,

                         ordered = VAR,

                         group = "Sex")

 

 

A comment on the usage of data in both commands. As highlighted above, measEq.syntax and cfa.mi use different data sources (BASELINE_IMP_EX_1 vs BASELINE_IMP_EX). The latter data set is actually the imputed data that I compiled by the means of using mice. The other data set is one of the individual datasets that were compiled. I exported all imputed data sets to separate data frames because I need them for something else. In general, one can use measEq.syntax without the data add-on. Doing so, however, causes problems later on. Since one cannot combine a mice mid object with measEq.syntax I used this ‘trick’. As a result, I was able to estimate the baseline model.

 

Similarly, I proceeded to estimate the threshold-invariance model:

 

prob4 <- measEq.syntax(configural.model = MODEL,

                       data = BASELINE_IMP_EX_1,

                       ordered = VAR,

                       parameterization = "delta",

                       ID.fac = "std.lv",

                       ID.cat = "Wu.Estabrook.2016",

                       group.equal = "thresholds",

                       group = "Sex")

 

model.prob4 <- as.character(prob4)

 

PROB4.FIT <- cfa.mi(model.prob4,

                    data=BASELINE_EX_IMP,

                    ordered = VAR,

                    group = "Sex")

 

If I now look at the fit indices I find that

 

Model - chisq.sc - df.sc - pvalue.sc - rmsea.sc - cfi.s - tli.sc

Confi    737.05         334             0              0.042      0.983     0.981

Thres    737.05         334            0               0.042      0.983     0.981

 

As already mentioned, this is weird.

 

Just to sum up, what has gone wrong?

 

Any help much appreciated.

 

Best,

 

Dom

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Analysis of Measurement Invariance with multiple imputed data and categorical variables
parts: the baseline and the thresholds models do not differ at all in terms of the fit indices and even in terms of df.

They are equivalent models when items have only 2 thresholds, because those 2 constraints (per indicator) are traded for 2 estimates (intercept and residual variance).  With 3-category indicators, threshold invariance can only be assumed, not tested, so you can treat that as your configural model.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
